notes: The image is a local build, made by the devcontainer CLI from bench/image/Dockerfile as statespace_devcontainer-bench and tagged statespace-bench:w0t05 here. Its digest is the image manifest's (with Docker's containerd image store and no attestation, the image ID); a registry digest exists only once CI pushes the image, and the nightly and monthly lanes read it from the repository variable BENCH_IMAGE (W0-T04). The devcontainer was brought up with STATESPACE_BENCH_IMAGE set to statespace-bench@sha256:b161b2a1d80430f47efa4f326db727f5c44e7a946ecd4aad4f13616b58a02e09, so the doctor report and its receipt block carry that digest. The cold build's manifest digest was sha256:8bf2a44a100313e0d87b7939ddcf0158e95c32b2efd1d858355946049142a94e, and the cached build's, the digest of record, is sha256:b161b2a1d80430f47efa4f326db727f5c44e7a946ecd4aad4f13616b58a02e09: they hold the same 21 layers and differ in the image config (checks cold-and-cached-builds-have-the-same-layers and devcontainer-up-reproduces-the-image-digest). The cause was not isolated in this run; in a scratch trial that is not recorded here, an image built with the argument BUILDKIT_INLINE_CACHE=1, which the devcontainer CLI passes, carried a moby.buildkit.cache.v0 entry in its config, and a cold and a cached build of a two-line Dockerfile differed in their IDs. A build in another place or at another time will have other layers, because they hold file times and the Ubuntu packages of the day.

The devcontainer CLI does not run the image byte for byte: it adds the labels of devcontainer.json to the built image (already part of statespace-bench@sha256:b161b2a1d80430f47efa4f326db727f5c44e7a946ecd4aad4f13616b58a02e09) and, because this host's user and the image's user differ in group id, one layer that sets the user ids. The container's image has 22 layers, and its first 21 are the built image's (check devcontainer-runs-the-built-layers).

The recorded build ran without the layer cache (devcontainer build --no-cache), in a clean copy of the working tree (2678 files: the tracked files and the untracked files that .gitignore lets through), so every download was checked against its pinned SHA-256 again and the last step of the Dockerfile, statespace doctor, ran on the fresh image. With the cache warm the same build takes seconds.

Sizes, each as its command reports it: docker image inspect Size 1663129890 bytes; docker images 7.63GB; du of the unpacked root file system 5799502321 bytes (a root-owned container reading its own tree); the sum of the layer sizes in docker history 5969502208 bytes. Which of them is a download size was not measured: no registry was involved.

Where the TLC jars ship: in the image at /opt/tla2tools/, copied by the Dockerfile from bench/image/tla2tools/ in the repository and checked against the SHA-256 values of RUN-tlc-jars. They are vendored because the v1.8.0 release is re-published under its tag: tla2tools-release-asset.json is the asset as the GitHub API listed it when this run was recorded, and it is not the jar the course ran (its SHA-256 differs from the pinned one).

The memory cap is applied with docker update after devcontainer up --skip-post-create and before devcontainer run-user-commands, so the postCreateCommand (statespace doctor) and every later command ran under the 6 GiB cap, on the devcontainer.json as shipped. The opt-in run uses a copy of devcontainer.json in which the one line named by its comment lists docker-compose.sandbox.yml too, with absolute paths.

The default devcontainer reports the sandbox as failed with the line W0-S06 recorded for default Docker, and the run is still green: the sandbox is recorded and never required. The opt-in profile starts it on this host, which has no AppArmor (RUN-bwrap-lanes). On an Ubuntu 24.04 host the profile is not enough; Codespaces and Docker Desktop were not run.

The pins of the Rust toolchain's binaries, of Java and of the Z3 wheel's files were first hashed by this run; every other hash is one that an earlier run recorded (the Lean toolchain's eight binaries by RUN-bwrap-lanes, the jars by RUN-tlc-jars, cvc5 and uv by RUN-scaffold, Soufflé by RUN-souffle-version).

Ubuntu packages (bubblewrap, git, build-essential, libclang-dev, openssh-client, unzip, less, and what Soufflé's package depends on) come from the Ubuntu 24.04 archive of the day and are not pinned by version; the image digest is what pins them.

Only linux/amd64 was built and run. The Dockerfile and the compose file force that platform, because every hash is the x86_64 build's; on Apple silicon Docker Desktop would run the image under emulation, which was not measured (W0-S06 owner action 3).
The build-time check leaves PostgreSQL out (a service container) and records the sandbox as off by choice, because the sandbox cannot start during a build.
The devcontainer CLI is run through npx at the version in the argv; its npm integrity value is in values.devcontainer_cli.
